lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A three-goal lead vanished into a 4-3 shootout loss, and with it went the easy fiction that these Maple Leafs have already found their shape. Jack Roslovic, Easton Cowan and Nick Paul struck in the first period, but Vegas answered with wave after wave, exposing a club still searching for chemistry. The defeat leaves Toronto 2-2-1, fifth in the Atlantic Division with five points and a one-game losing streak - hardly a crisis, but plainly unfinished business. Worse, Oliver Ekman-Larsson left late after a hit from Jeremy Lauzon and did not return; coach Jim Hiller had no update. Toronto now heads into Colorado with more questions than polish. Saturday's 7 p.m. visit to the Avalanche will test whether this team can protect a lead, support its defence and turn early promise into a complete night.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season ended with the Blue Jays 79-83 and fifth in the AL East, but the real work begins now: repairing an offense that left too much responsibility on Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Joey Votto's blunt prescription for Guerrero - "Watch your dad" - puts the club's central problem in plain English: Toronto needs its star first baseman's plate approach, not merely his reputation, to rebound. The more encouraging development is Kazuma Okamoto's breakthrough, which has given the Jays credibility in Japan and prompted plans for a winter delegation there. That is smart baseball and smart business. Still, Toronto needs more than international ambition. It needs lineup balance, dependable pitching and a coherent answer at the infield corners. Chasing a splash such as Jazz Chisholm Jr. may entertain, but fit and price matter more than headlines. Watch this winter for whether Ross Atkins builds around Guerrero and Okamoto - or asks them to carry another incomplete roster.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors' preseason has already exposed the central tension: promise is plentiful, certainty is not. The 129-105 loss to Miami on Oct. 3 was an exhibition defeat, not a verdict, but it sharpened the scrutiny on Darko Rajakovic as he tries to turn a young, versatile roster into a disciplined nine-man rotation. Kyle Anderson is the most intriguing addition - a 6-foot-8 connective passer and defender whose value will be measured less in points than in whether he settles the second unit and helps Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett and the emerging Jamal Shead play faster without playing loose. Barrett's description of Shead as the team's "heart and soul" says plenty about the guard's influence. Anderson's knee bruise has cleared, and he should be available. Saturday's preseason meeting with the Clippers at 6:30 p.m. ET is the next audition, before Toronto opens the regular season against Chicago on Oct. 21.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season is already fraying at the edges, and London only pulled the thread. Sunday's 30-13 loss to Indianapolis dropped Washington to 1-3, fourth in the NFC East and two games behind, with a one-game losing streak now attached to a team that has lost three of four. The injury list has become its own opponent: 23 players appeared on it, 17 limited or absent Wednesday, while Marcus Mariota's knee injury leaves rookie Athan Kaliakmanis as the backup. There is, at least, a lifeline. Jayden Daniels is "full go" after missing two games with an elbow injury, but Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both carry hamstring concerns. This is how another Commanders season begins to unravel - not with one collapse, but with a roster steadily hollowed out. Sunday's 1 p.m. Fox meeting with the 3-1 Giants is less a rescue mission than a test of whether Daniels can stop the slide.

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose 4-3 After Blowing Lead
paragraphs: The Leafs let a three-goal advantage disappear Thursday, losing 4-3 to the Golden Knights. Easton Cowan, Nick Paul and Jack Roslovic scored, while Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 40 shots for a .930 save percentage. Toronto is 2-2-1 and fifth in the Atlantic Division, with Colorado next Saturday at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet.

The Blue Jays head toward the offseason with five major needs identified by MLB.com, while Sportsnet examines how Wataru Okamoto's success could support the club's push into Japan. The Raptors face the Clippers in a preseason game Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET, then open the regular season against the Bulls on Wednesday, October 21, at 7:30 p.m. ET. Kyle Anderson's role remains a focus as scrutiny builds around Darko Rajakovic.

The Commanders, 1-3 and fourth in the NFC East, host the Giants Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Washington's season has drawn sharper questions, while Dallas owner Jerry Jones has expressed confidence in Christian Parker.
